summary: Source decomposition of the geometric-modular-forms and Serre-weight chain from four primary sources actually read: Katz's LNM 350 paper for the sheaf omega with its Tate-curve normalization, the q-expansion principles (ordinary and strong), base change with its weight-one boundary, integral Hecke operators, the Hasse invariant and Deligne's congruence with the p = 2, 3 exceptions; Edixhoven's paper for the theta operator, the filtration, theta-cycles, weight reduction to at most p+1, the finiteness-at-p criterion and the comparison of his k(rho) with Serre's k_rho; Serre's Duke paper for the full piecewise local weight recipe (tame level 1 and 2, wild peu/tres ramifie), the determinant and parity relations, and the k = 2 finite-flat criterion; Deligne-Serre for the eigenvalue-lifting lemma, the Eisenstein weight shift, and realizability over the field of characteristic polynomials; and Raynaud Bull. SMF 102 (1974) section 3 for the prolongation and tame-character results that Serre's k = 2 criterion imports. Reading Raynaud identified the precise reason Serre's Proposition 4 is proved only for p different from 2 (uniqueness of the finite flat model needs e < p-1, i.e. p >= 3 over Z_p) and showed that Serre's printed citation 'Raynaud [35], th. 2.4.3' has no referent in Raynaud 1974, the intended result being Theorem 3.4.3. Boundaries that the sources do not close are recorded as gaps rather than as inputs: Serre's Proposition 4 at p = 2, the unread Raynaud and Katz-LNM-601 imports, Fontaine's and Gross's theorems, and the GAGA comparison.

nodes.title: The invertible sheaf omega on the compactified level-n moduli scheme, normalized at the Tate curve
nodes.statement: For n >= 1 there is a unique invertible sheaf omega on the compactified modular scheme Mbar_n over Z[1/n] whose restriction to M_n is omega_{E/M_n} for the universal elliptic curve with level-n structure, and whose sections over the completion Z[1/n, zeta_n][[q]] at each cusp are exactly the Z[1/n, zeta_n][[q]]-multiples of the canonical differential of the Tate curve. The Kodaira-Spencer map extends to an isomorphism omega^{tensor 2} = Omega^1_{Mbar_n / Z[1/n]}(log(cusps)), and over Z[1/n, zeta_n][[q]] the square of the canonical differential of Tate(q^n) corresponds to n dq/q. A modular form of level n and weight k holomorphic at infinity over a Z[1/n]-algebra R_0, resp. with coefficients in a Z[1/n]-module K, is a global section of omega^{tensor k} on Mbar_n tensor R_0, resp. an element of H^0(Mbar_n, omega^{tensor k} tensor_{Z[1/n]} K).
hypotheses: n invertible on the base: all schemes are over Z[1/n]
the universal object is an elliptic curve with level-n structure on M_n, extended to the compactification Mbar_n by Tate curves at the cusps
the cusp normalization is fixed by the Tate curve Tate(q^n) over Z[1/n, zeta_n][[q]] together with its canonical differential
the Kodaira-Spencer identification carries the factor n: the square of the canonical differential on Tate(q^n) corresponds to n dq/q, not to dq/q
proofSteps: Katz 1.5 constructs omega by the stated two conditions (restriction to M_n, and prescribed sections at each cusp) and asserts uniqueness.
The Kodaira-Spencer isomorphism omega^{tensor 2} = Omega^1(log cusps) of A1.3.17 is extended across the cusps; Katz records the explicit q-form of the identification for Tate(q^n).
Modular forms holomorphic at infinity are then defined as sections of omega^{tensor k}, with coefficients in an arbitrary Z[1/n]-module K by tensoring the sheaf.

nodes.title: Level one and level two forms as invariants of a rigidifying cover, with the primes that must be inverted
nodes.statement: For n = 1, 2 the module S(K, n, k) of weight-k forms holomorphic at infinity with coefficients in a Z[1/n]-module K is defined not as sections over a coarse space but by descent from the rigid levels: for n = 2 as the subgroup of H^0(Mbar_4, omega^{tensor k} tensor_{Z[1/4]} K) invariant under the matrices of GL_2(Z/4Z) that are congruent to 1 mod 2, and for n = 1 as the fibre product of the level-3 and level-4 modules over the level-12 module. Base change then holds in the form: S(Z[1/2], 2, k) tensor R_0 -> S(R_0, 2, k) is an isomorphism for every ring R_0 in which 2 is invertible and every k >= 1, and S(Z[1/6], 1, k) tensor R_0 -> S(R_0, 1, k) is an isomorphism for every ring R_0 in which 2 and 3 are invertible. These statements are false without inverting 2 and 3.
hypotheses: for level 2: 2 invertible in R_0; for level 1: 2 and 3 invertible in R_0

the descent uses that the relevant rigidifying groups (order 16 for the mod-2 congruence subgroup of GL_2(Z/4Z), 96 for GL_2(Z/4Z), 48 for GL_2(Z/3Z)) have order invertible after inverting 2 and 3, so an averaging projector exists
level-two forms of odd weight vanish because the automorphism -1 of an elliptic curve fixes the level-two structure
proofSteps: Katz Thm 1.8.1: level-two forms over R_0 containing 1/2 are exactly the level-four forms invariant under the mod-2 congruence subgroup of GL_2(Z/4Z); that group has order 16, a power of 2, so the averaging projector applies to the level-four base-change isomorphism of Thm 1.7.1.

Katz Thm 1.8.2: over a ring containing 1/6 the same projector argument reduces level one to GL_2(Z/4Z)- or GL_2(Z/3Z)-invariants; the passage from Z[1/6] down to Z uses the fibre-product description 1.8.2.1 of level-one forms and the fact that fibre products commute with flat base change.

nodes.title: The q-expansion principle at level n >= 3 and its underlying vanishing theorem
nodes.statement: Let n >= 3, K a Z[1/n]-module, and f a modular form of level n and weight k holomorphic at infinity with coefficients in K. (Vanishing) If on each of the phi(n) connected components of Mbar_n tensor_{Z[1/n]} Z[1/n, zeta_n] there is at least one cusp at which the q-expansion of f vanishes identically, then f = 0. (q-expansion principle) If L is a Z[1/n]-submodule of K and on each of those phi(n) components there is at least one cusp at which all q-coefficients of f lie in L tensor_{Z[1/n]} Z[1/n, zeta_n], then f is a modular form with coefficients in L. For n = 1, 2 the same conclusion holds after testing at a single cusp (one cusp when n = 1, one of the three cusps when n = 2).
hypotheses: n >= 3 for the stated component-wise form; n = 1 or 2 for Cor. 1.9.1, where the modules S(K, n, k) are the descent-theoretic ones
K is a Z[1/n]-module and L a Z[1/n]-submodule; no flatness or finiteness on K is assumed
the test cusps must meet every one of the phi(n) geometric connected components of Mbar_n over Z[1/n, zeta_n]; a single cusp does not suffice at level n >= 3

nodes.title: Base change for spaces of modular forms, and the unresolved weight-one case for n >= 13
nodes.statement: Let n >= 3 and suppose either k >= 2, or k = 1 and n <= 11. Then for any Z[1/n]-module K the canonical map K tensor H^0(Mbar_n, omega^{tensor k}) -> H^0(Mbar_n, K tensor omega^{tensor k}) is an isomorphism. The proof is by H^1(Mbar_n, omega^{tensor k}) = 0, which follows from Riemann-Roch once deg(omega^{tensor k}) > 2g-2 on each geometric component, using omega^{tensor 2} = Omega^1(log cusps) and the fact that each component of Mbar_n tensor Z[1/n, zeta_n] contains a cusp. For k = 1 and n = 12 the degree of omega equals 2g-2 and Katz records that he does not know whether formation of weight-one forms of level n > 12 commutes with base change.
hypotheses: n >= 3, so that Mbar_n is a scheme and the universal curve exists
k >= 2, or k = 1 with 3 <= n <= 11
the vanishing argument needs each connected component of Mbar_n tensor Z[1/n, zeta_n] to contain at least one cusp
proofSteps: Katz Thm 1.7.1 reduces base change to H^1(Mbar_n, omega^{tensor k}) = 0 by the standard cohomology and base-change theorems.
For k >= 2 the isomorphism omega^{tensor 2} = Omega^1_{Z[1/n]}(log(cusps)) plus the presence of a cusp on each component gives deg(omega^{tensor k}) > 2g-2, hence the vanishing by Riemann-Roch.
For k = 1 and 3 <= n <= 11 an explicit degree computation gives the same inequality; at n = 12 equality holds and the argument stops.

nodes.title: The Hasse invariant as a level-one weight-(p-1) form over F_p with q-expansion 1
nodes.statement: Let R be an F_p-algebra and E/R an elliptic curve. Absolute Frobenius induces a p-linear endomorphism of H^1(E, O_E); if omega is a basis of omega_{E/R} with dual basis eta of H^1(E, O_E), define A(E, omega) in R by F_abs(eta) = A(E, omega) eta. Then A(E, k omega) = k^{1-p} A(E, omega) for k in R^*, so A is a modular form of level one and weight p-1 over F_p. Intrinsically A is the section of omega_{E/R}^{tensor (p-1)} corresponding to the R-linear map F_abs: (H^1(E,O_E))^{tensor p} -> H^1(E, O_E). A is holomorphic at infinity and A(Tate(q), omega_can) = 1.
hypotheses: R is an F_p-algebra (p = 0 in R); the construction is purely characteristic p
omega must be a basis of omega_{E/R}, so the scalar A(E, omega) is defined only after a trivialization, the weight p-1 transformation law being exactly the resulting ambiguity
holomorphy at infinity uses that the Tate curve over F_p((q)) extends to a plane curve over F_p[[q]] whose dualizing sheaf has omega_can as a basis

He reinterprets F_abs as an R-linear map on the p-th tensor power, exhibiting A as a section of omega^{tensor (p-1)}.

nodes.title: A = E_{p-1} mod p for p >= 5, and the explicit level-n liftings of A required at p = 2, 3
nodes.statement: For p >= 5 the Eisenstein series E_{p-1} of level one and weight p-1 has p-integral q-expansion coefficients (the p-adic ordinal of 2(p-1)/B_{p-1} is 1) and reduces mod p to a level-one weight-(p-1) form with constant q-expansion 1; since two level-one forms of the same weight with the same q-expansion coincide, A = E_{p-1} mod p. For p = 2 and p = 3 no lifting of A to a level-one form holomorphic at infinity over a p-adic ring exists; instead, for p = 2 and odd n with 3 <= n <= 11, A lifts to a weight-1 level-n form holomorphic at infinity over Z[1/n], and for p = 3 and any n >= 3 with 3 not dividing n, A lifts to a weight-2 level-n form over Z[1/n], both by Theorem 1.7.1. Katz records that he does not know whether A lifts to level n for p = 2 and other n (even n = 13), and notes that E_4 provides a level-one lifting of A^4 when p = 2 and of A^2 when p = 3.

nodes.title: The theta operator, the filtration w(f), and their Hecke commutation relations
nodes.statement: Let M(N) = direct sum over k >= 0 of M(N, k), the graded F_p-bar-algebra of mod p modular forms of level N. The filtration of f in M(N, k) is w(f) = min{ k - i(p-1) : f is in A^i M(N, k - i(p-1)) } where A is the Hasse invariant; equivalently w(f) is the least k' such that some form of weight k' has, at some cusp, the same q-expansion as f. This equivalence rests on the fact that the kernel of the q-expansion map M(N) -> F_p-bar[[q]] at any cusp is the ideal generated by A - 1. There is a derivation theta: M(N) -> M(N) raising degrees by p+1 whose effect on q-expansions at all cusps is q d/dq. If f in M(N, k) has filtration k and p does not divide k, then w(theta f) = k + p + 1. If f is in M(N, pk) and theta f = 0, then f = g^p for a unique g in M(N, k). The Hecke commutation is T_l^*(theta f) = l theta(T_l^* f), so in particular T_p^*(theta f) = 0, and if f is an eigenform of type (N, k, eps) with eigenvalues a_l then theta f is an eigenform of type (N, k+p+1, eps) with eigenvalues l a_l, whence rho_{theta f} = rho_f tensor chi.

The eigenvalue statement l a_l is the twist by the cyclotomic character, which is what makes rho_{theta f} = rho_f tensor chi.

nodes.title: Tate's theta-cycles, with the p > 3 classification and the explicit p = 2 and p = 3 tables
nodes.statement: For a homogeneous f in M(N) with theta f nonzero, the theta-cycle of f is the sequence (w(theta f), ..., w(theta^{p-1} f)). Up to cyclic permutation a theta-cycle is always of one of the two displayed shapes: (k, k+p+1, ..., k+(p-2)(p+1)) when k = 2 mod p, and (k, k+p+1, ..., k+(p-k_0)(p+1), k_1, k_1+p+1, ..., k_1+(k_0-3)(p+1)) when k = k_0 mod p with 3 <= k_0 <= (p+3)/2 and k_1 = k + p + 3 - 2 k_0 - this classification being asserted at least for p > 3. For p = 2 the only possibility is (k) with k = 0 mod 2; for p = 3 the possibilities are (k, k+4) with k = 2 mod 3 and (k, k) with k = 0 mod 3. For a cuspidal eigenform of type (N, k, eps) with 1 <= k <= p+1 and w(f) = k, the cycle is given by the case table of Prop. 3.3, which splits on whether a_p = 0 and has explicit small-characteristic variants for p = 2 and p = 3.

nodes.title: The two tame characters of a local residual representation are of level 1 or of level 2 and then conjugate
nodes.statement: Let rho_p: G_p -> GL(V) = GL_2(F_p-bar) be continuous, G_p = Gal(Qbar_p/Q_p), I its inertia subgroup, I_p the wild inertia (the maximal pro-p subgroup of I) and I_t = I/I_p the tame quotient. On the semisimplification V^{ss} of V as a G_p-module, I_p acts trivially, so I_t acts and the action is diagonalizable, given by two characters phi, phi' of I_t. These characters are of level 1 or of level 2; if they are of level 2 then phi' = phi^p and phi = phi'^p. When phi, phi' are of level 2, V is irreducible.
hypotheses: V is 2-dimensional over F_p-bar and rho_p is continuous, so its image is finite
I_p acts trivially on V^{ss}: this is the standard fact that a pro-p group acting on a semisimple F_p-bar-representation of a p-group quotient acts trivially, cited by Serre as [41], prop. 4
the identification I_t = inverse limit of F_{p^n}^* is cited as [41], prop. 2
proofSteps: Choose s in G_p lifting the Frobenius x -> x^p of G_p/I = Gal(F_p-bar/F_p). Serre checks that s u s^{-1} = u^p mod I_p for u in I, so conjugation by s acts on I_t by u -> u^p.

Hence the set {phi, phi'} is stable under p-th power, giving the dichotomy: either phi^p = phi and phi'^p = phi' (both of level 1), or phi^p = phi', phi'^p = phi with phi different from phi' (both of level 2).
In the level-2 case V is irreducible: a stable line would give a character of I_t extendable to G_p, hence of level 1.

nodes.title: Serre's weight in the two tame cases, with the normalizations and the (0,0) shift
nodes.statement: Level-2 case (Serre 2.2): if phi, phi' are of level 2, write phi = psi^a psi'^b uniquely with 0 <= a, b <= p-1 using the two fundamental characters psi, psi' of level 2; then b is different from a (else phi would be chi^a, of level 1), and after permuting phi and phi' one may assume 0 <= a < b <= p-1; set k = 1 + pa + b. Level-1 tame case (Serre 2.3): if I acts semisimply on V through chi^a and chi^b, normalize 0 <= a, b <= p-2 and a <= b; set k = 1 + pa + b if (a,b) is not (0,0), and k = p if (a,b) = (0,0). The value k = p in the unramified case is a deliberate shift by p-1 away from the formula's value 1, chosen by Serre to avoid weight-one forms. Twisting: rho_p = chi^a tensor rho_p' has (a,b) replaced by (0, b-a) with weight k' = 1 + b - a, so k = k' + a(p+1).

nodes.title: The wildly ramified case: the peu ramifie / tres ramifie dichotomy and the weight it produces
nodes.statement: Suppose I_p acts nontrivially on V. Then D = V^{I_p} is a line, stable under G_p, and G_p acts on V/D by a character theta_1 and on D by theta_2. Write theta_1 = chi^alpha eps_1, theta_2 = chi^beta eps_2 with eps_i unramified and normalize 0 <= alpha <= p-2 and 1 <= beta <= p-1 (the two exponents do NOT play symmetric roles). Put a = min(alpha, beta), b = max(alpha, beta). If beta is not alpha+1, set k = 1 + pa + b. If beta = alpha+1, then Gal(K_t/K_0) = (Z/pZ)^* with K_t = K_0(zeta_p), K/K_t is elementary abelian of exponent p and by Kummer theory K = K_t(x_1^{1/p}, ..., x_m^{1/p}) with x_i in K_0^*/K_0^{*p}; rho_p is called peu ramifie if v_p(x_i) = 0 mod p for all i (the x_i can be chosen to be units) and tres ramifie otherwise. In the peu ramifie case k = 1 + pa + b = 2 + a(p+1); in the tres ramifie case one adds p-1 (resp. 2 if p = 2), giving k = (a+1)(p+1) for p different from 2 and k = 4 for p = 2. Serre notes that the tres ramifie case forces eps_1 = eps_2 and then m = 1 or 2.

the peu/tres dichotomy is a condition on the extension class, not on the semisimplification: it is read off from the valuations of the Kummer generators x_i in K_0^* = (Q_p^{nr})^*

nodes.title: det rho_p restricted to inertia is chi^{k-1}, and the global parity relation eps(-1) = (-1)^k
nodes.statement: For every case of Serre's recipe, det rho_p restricted to I equals chi^{k-1}; since chi restricted to I has order p-1, the class of k mod (p-1) is determined by det rho_p, and indeed by its restriction to inertia alone. Equivalently det rho_p = eps_p chi^{k-1} with eps_p an unramified F_p-bar^*-valued character of G_p, and when rho_p comes from a global rho the character eps_p is the p-component of eps, with eps_p(Frob_p) = eps(p). Globally, det rho is a character of (Z/pNZ)^*, decomposing as chi^h times eps with h = k-1 mod (p-1), det rho(Frob_l) = l^{k-1} eps(l) for l not dividing pN, and det rho(c) = (-1)^{k-1} eps(-1); the oddness hypothesis det rho(c) = -1 is therefore equivalent to eps(-1) = (-1)^k. For p = 2 oddness is automatic since -1 = 1.

In the case {1, chi} one takes the unique finite flat prolongation J over Z_p (Raynaud prop. 3.3.2), which is reducible, and gets an exact sequence 0 -> A -> J -> B -> 0 of finite flat group schemes of order p with one of A, B etale and the other multiplicative; after a finite etale extension R of Z_p the sequence becomes 0 -> Z/pZ -> J -> mu_p -> 0 or 0 -> mu_p -> J -> Z/pZ -> 0.

In the first case the identity component splits the extension and I_p acts trivially; in the second the Kummer sequence gives a class u in R^*/R^{*p} with u a unit, so K/K_t is unramified or peu ramifie; either way k = 2.
For the converse, the level-2 branch is Raynaud [35] thm. 2.4.3 and the level-1 branch is a direct construction over an auxiliary finite etale extension R of Z_p followed by descent to Z_p.

nodes.statement: Let F be a finite extension of F_p and rho_p: G_p -> GL_2(F) continuous and upper triangular with diagonal (chi theta_2, theta_1), theta_1 and theta_2 unramified F^*-valued characters of G_p. Let V_{Q_p} be the F-vector space scheme over Q_p attached to rho_p and D the integral closure of Z_p in the maximal unramified extension K of Q_p inside Qbar_p. Then the following are equivalent: rho_p is peu ramifie in Serre's sense (2.4.7); V_{Q_p} extends to a finite flat F-vector space scheme over D; over Z_p; extends to a finite flat group scheme over D; over Z_p. When these hold one says rho_p is finite. Moreover, in the peu ramifie case with p > 2, the Kummer classes [x_{i,j}] in D^*/D^{*p} satisfy [x_{i,j}] = (phi^*)^i [x_{0,j}] and their images y under D^*/D^{*p} = U/U^p = F_p-bar satisfy f(Frob_p)(y) = 0 for f the minimal polynomial of gamma = (theta_1 theta_2^{-1})(Frob_p); this equation has exactly p^s solutions in F_{p^n}, where s = [F_p(gamma):F_p] and n is the order of gamma.

nodes.title: Edixhoven's k(rho_p), its exact difference from Serre's k_rho, and the minimality theorem
nodes.statement: Edixhoven defines k(rho_p) by the same case division as Serre except in the reducible tame case, where the normalization is 0 <= a <= b <= p-2 with k(rho_p) = 1 + pa + b including (a,b) = (0,0) (so k(rho_p) = 1 for rho_p unramified), and in the wild case, where the additional p-1 is added exactly when chi^{beta - alpha} = chi and rho_p tensor chi^{-alpha} is not finite at p. Remark 4.4: always k(rho) <= k_rho, and they differ in exactly two cases - (i) rho_p|I_p trivial with a = b = 0, where k(rho) = 1 and k_rho = p; (ii) p = 2, rho_p|I_p nontrivial, alpha = 0, beta = 1 and rho_p not finite at p, where k(rho) = 3 and k_rho = 4. Theorem 4.5: if rho is continuous irreducible odd and isomorphic to rho_g for some cusp form g of type (N, k, eps) with p not dividing N, then there is a cuspidal eigenform f of type (N, k_rho, eps) with the same T_l^* eigenvalues for l different from p and rho isomorphic to rho_f; if moreover rho is not exceptional (rho_p not an extension of an unramified character by itself), there is such an f of type (N, k(rho), eps), and no eigenform of level prime to p and weight less than k(rho) has associated representation rho.
hypotheses: k(rho_p) is defined for a local representation and depends only on rho_p; the 'not finite at p' clause refers to the finiteness notion of section 8 of the source, i.e. existence of a finite flat model
Thm 4.5 assumes rho already modular of some type (N, k, eps) with p not dividing N; it is a weight-optimisation statement, not an existence statement

the minimality assertion and the k(rho) form of the conclusion require rho to be non-exceptional; the added end-of-introduction note states that for p > 2 the Coleman-Voloch result removes this condition
the proof depends on Gross [10] whose Hecke-equivariance compatibilities on pages 504-505 were, at the time of writing, unchecked; Coleman verified the map in (16.6)
proofSteps: Edixhoven Def. 4.3 gives the case division; Remark 4.4 compares it with Serre's k_rho and isolates the two discrepancies.

Proof of Thm 4.5: by Thm 3.4 there is alpha with rho tensor chi^{-alpha} isomorphic to rho_{f_1} for an eigenform f_1 of type (N, k_1, eps) with k_1 <= p+1 and w(f_1) = k_1; the local results Thms 2.5, 2.6, 2.8 and Prop. 2.7 then pin down k_1 and alpha in terms of rho|G_p.
The desired f is obtained by untwisting: apply theta alpha times and divide by the Hasse invariant as often as possible.

The main complication is that k_1 is not unique: a companion form of weight p+1-k_1 may exist (Gross, Thm 2.9) or f_1 may be a multiple of the Hasse invariant (only for k_1 = p or p+1; the k_1 = p+1 case is Mazur's Thm 2.8, which is where 'finite at p' enters).

nodes.title: Deligne-Serre eigenvalue lifting: eigenvalues lift, eigenvectors need not
nodes.statement: Let M be a finitely generated free module over a discrete valuation ring O with maximal ideal m, residue field k and fraction field K. Let T be a set of pairwise commuting endomorphisms of M. Let f in M/mM be a nonzero common eigenvector of the T in T, with eigenvalues a_T in k. Then there exist a discrete valuation ring O' containing O, with maximal ideal m' satisfying O intersect m' = m and fraction field K' finite over K, and a nonzero element f' of M' = O' tensor_O M which is an eigenvector of the T in T with eigenvalues a'_T satisfying a'_T = a_T mod m'. The source stresses that one does not assert that eigenvectors lift, only eigenvalues.
hypotheses: M must be free of finite type over O; this is where the base-change and finite-generation statements for spaces of modular forms are consumed
the endomorphisms in T must commute pairwise, but no self-adjointness or semisimplicity is assumed
the conclusion allows a finite extension O' of O: the lifted eigenvalues live in a possibly larger residue field, and only their reductions are controlled
proofSteps: Let H be the subalgebra of End(M) generated by T. After a finite scalar extension one may assume K tensor H is a product of artinian rings with residue field K.

Let chi: H -> k be the character with h f = chi(h) f. Since H is free over O there is a prime ideal p of H contained in the maximal ideal ker(chi) with p intersect O = 0; p is the kernel of a homomorphism chi': H -> O' reducing mod m to chi.

The ideal of K tensor H generated by p lies in the support of K tensor M, so there is a nonzero f'' in K tensor M annihilated by it, i.e. h f'' = chi'(h) f''; take f' a nonzero O'-multiple of f'' lying in M'.

The source also gives a Variante: reduce to M indecomposable under T with eigenvalues in K, produce a basis in which all T are upper triangular, and use indecomposability to force T_{ii} = a_T mod m for all i, so that f' = e_1 works.
acceptance: Check on an explicit non-semisimple Hecke module that the eigenvector does not lift but the eigenvalue system does
Check that the extension O' is genuinely needed by exhibiting a mod p eigensystem whose characteristic-zero lift has coefficients in a ramified extension

nodes.title: The Raynaud inputs to the k = 2 criterion, and why they degenerate exactly at p = 2
nodes.statement: Let R be a strictly henselian discrete valuation ring of mixed characteristic with absolute ramification index e, fraction field K of characteristic zero, residue characteristic p. (Prolongation and uniqueness, Raynaud Prop. 3.3.2) Let G be a K-scheme in F-vector spaces of rank q admitting a finite flat prolongation. If e < p-1 then the prolongation is unique up to isomorphism and is an F-vector space scheme; if e = p-1 and G is simple then either the prolongation is unique or there are exactly two, one etale and one of multiplicative type, and in all cases they are F-vector space schemes. (Tame characters, Raynaud Thm 3.4.1 and Cor. 3.4.4) Galois acts on G(Kbar) through a character psi = product of psi_j^{n_j}; if G is a Jordan-Holder quotient of a K-group scheme killed by a power of p that admits a finite flat prolongation over R, then psi = product psi_j^{n_j} with 0 <= n_j <= e. (Full faithfulness, Cor. 3.3.6) If e < p-1, every morphism of generic fibres extends uniquely, the kernel and cokernel of the extension are flat over R, and Ext^1 of finite flat group schemes injects into Ext^1 of their generic fibres. Consequence for the Serre recipe: for R = Z_p^{nr} one has e = 1, so the constraint 0 <= n, n' <= 1 on the tame characters holds for every p, but the uniqueness statement 3.3.2.2 requires 1 < p-1, i.e. p >= 3; at p = 2 one is exactly in the case e = p-1 of 3.3.2.3 and uniqueness of the finite flat model may fail.
hypotheses: R strictly henselian, mixed characteristic, K of characteristic zero - Raynaud's standing hypotheses in section 3
Prop. 3.3.2.2 needs e < p-1; Prop. 3.3.2.3 covers e = p-1 and additionally requires G simple and R henselian
Cor. 3.4.4 needs only that G admits a finite flat prolongation; the bound on the exponents is 0 <= n_j <= e, so it is informative only for e < p-1 (Raynaud's Remark 3.4.6 says so explicitly)
Cor. 3.3.6 needs e < p-1 and both group schemes commutative, finite, flat and killed by a power of p
proofSteps: Raynaud's Prop. 3.3.2.1 characterizes the maximal prolongation by the conditions v(delta_i) <= p-1 for all i and v(delta_i) < p-1 for some i on the equations of type (1); 2 and 3 follow by comparing the maximal and minimal F-vector space prolongations.

Thm 3.4.1 computes the Galois action on G(Kbar) as a homothety through psi = psi_0^{v(delta_0)} ... psi_{r-1}^{v(delta_{r-1})}; Thm 3.4.3 turns prolongability into the condition 0 <= n_j <= e using Prop. 3.3.2 to extend the F-structure to the prolongation.
Cor. 3.4.4 combines 3.2.1 (existence of a Jordan-Holder filtration with F-vector space quotients) with 3.4.3.
Cor. 3.3.6 is deduced from Thm 3.3.3, itself a consequence of Prop. 3.3.2.2 via the devissage of Prop. 3.2.1.

nodes.title: Residual modularity: mod p cusp forms of type (N, k, eps), the chosen place above p, and the field of coefficients
nodes.statement: Fix N >= 1 prime to p, k >= 2 and a character eps: (Z/NZ)^* -> F_p-bar^* with eps(-1) = (-1)^k for p different from 2 and k even for p = 2. Embed Qbar in C and choose a place of Qbar above p, giving a reduction map from the ring of algebraic integers to F_p-bar; let eps_0 be the multiplicative (Teichmuller) lift of eps. A cusp form of type (N, k, eps) with coefficients in F_p-bar is a formal series f = sum_{n >= 1} a_n q^n that is the reduction of some classical cusp form F = sum A_n q^n of type (N, k, eps_0) with algebraic integer coefficients. The space S(N, k, eps) does not depend on the chosen p-adic place and has F_p-bar-dimension equal to the complex dimension of S(N, k, eps_0); it is stable under T_l (l not dividing pN) and U_l (l | pN), with U_p the reduction of T_p using k >= 2; a normalized eigenform is determined by its eigenvalues a_l through the usual Euler product. Edixhoven records that in [27] Serre replaced this definition by Katz's, which is a priori larger and allows weight 1.
hypotheses: N prime to p and k >= 2 in this definition; the level-p case is not excluded mathematically but yields no genuinely new mod p forms, at the cost of raising the weight
the parity condition eps(-1) = (-1)^k is imposed, and is automatic at p = 2 where instead k is required even
the reduction of T_p to U_p uses k >= 2 so that the term eps_0(p) p^{k-1} vanishes mod p
the dimension comparison 3.1.3 is imported from Shimura [51] Thm 3.52 (also Deligne-Serre [11] Prop. 2.7) and is not reproved in the source

3.1.3: independence of the chosen place and the equality of dimensions, quoted from Shimura Thm 3.52.
3.1.4: stability under T_l and U_l with explicit q-expansion formulas; the U_p case uses k >= 2.
3.1.5: normalization a_1 = 1, commutation of Hecke operators, and the Euler product showing f is determined by the a_l.
3.1.6: every mod p eigensystem lifts to a characteristic-zero normalized eigenform, by the eigenvalue lifting lemma cited as [11] lemme 6.11 - i.e. the node deligne-serre-eigenvalue-lifting-lemma.
3.1.7: Deligne's theorem attaches to a normalized eigenform f a continuous semisimple rho_f, unramified outside pN, with Tr rho_f(Frob_l) = a_l and det rho_f(Frob_l) = eps(l) l^{k-1}.

nodes.title: A semisimple representation over a finite field is realizable over the subfield generated by its characteristic polynomials
nodes.statement: Let phi: Phi -> GL_n(k') be a semisimple representation of a group Phi over a finite field k', and let k be a subfield of k' containing the coefficients of the polynomials det(1 - phi(s)T) for all s in Phi. Then phi is realizable over k, i.e. isomorphic to a representation Phi -> GL_n(k). The proof: it suffices that phi be isomorphic to sigma(phi) for every k-automorphism sigma of k', because the Brauer group of a finite field is trivial so there is no Schur index; and phi and sigma(phi) have the same characteristic polynomials and are semisimple, hence isomorphic by Curtis-Reiner Thm 30.16.
hypotheses: k' finite and phi semisimple; both are used, semisimplicity through the character-determines-representation theorem and finiteness through the vanishing of the Brauer group
the hypothesis is on the coefficients of all characteristic polynomials, not merely on traces; in residual characteristic 2 traces alone are insufficient
in Deligne-Serre's application the field k_f is generated by the eigenvalues a_p and the reductions of eps(p), and Cebotarev is used to see that every element of the image is a Frobenius
proofSteps: Deligne-Serre 6.12 produces a semisimple mod-lambda representation phi whose characteristic polynomials have coefficients in k_f, by Cebotarev plus the definition of k_f.
Lemme 6.13 then descends the field of definition, via triviality of the Brauer group of a finite field and Curtis-Reiner Thm 30.16.

nodes.title: The weight-and-level target: the statement to which the recipe is attached
nodes.statement: Let rho: G_Q -> GL(V) = GL_2(F_p-bar) be continuous with (3.2.1) rho irreducible and (3.2.2) det rho odd. The qualitative statement (3.2.3?) is that rho is isomorphic to rho_f for some mod p Hecke eigenform f; the refined statement (3.2.4?) is that f can be taken of type (N, k, eps) with N the prime-to-p Artin conductor of rho, k the weight of section 2 and eps the character of 1.3. For a normalized f this means Tr rho(Frob_l) = a_l and det rho(Frob_l) = eps(l) l^{k-1} for all l not dividing pN - and the trace identity on a set of l of density 1 already suffices. Serre further conjectures (3.2.6?) that for l dividing pN, a_l is nonzero exactly when rho restricted to the decomposition group at l has a 1-dimensional unramified quotient V/D, in which case a_l is the Frobenius eigenvalue on V/D; for l | N such a D is unique, and the same holds for l = p when rho is ramified at p, whereas for rho unramified at p (so k = p by Serre's convention) there are two possible a_p, the two Frobenius eigenvalues, with product eps(p).
hypotheses: rho irreducible and det rho odd - both are hypotheses of the statement, not conclusions
N is the prime-to-p part of the Artin conductor: n(l, rho) = dim V/V^{G_0} + b(V) where b is the wild invariant, so N is a genuine conductor and not merely a ramification set
Serre's remark (5) that N and k are minimal is stated as probable, not proved, in the source; minimality of the weight is proved separately by Edixhoven Thm 4.5 under the non-exceptional hypothesis
the a_p statements at l = p distinguish sharply between rho ramified and unramified at p
proofSteps: Serre 1.2 defines n(l, rho) by (1.2.1) and rewrites it as (1.2.2) dim V/V^{G_0} + b(V), and deduces that n(l, rho) = 0 exactly when rho is unramified at l and n(l, rho) = dim V/V^{G_0} exactly when rho is tamely ramified at l.
3.2 states the conjecture in its qualitative and refined forms and translates the isomorphism rho = rho_f into the trace and determinant identities (3.2.5).
Remarks (1)-(3) analyse the local eigenvalue a_l for l | pN, including the criterion v_l(N) = 1 or v_l(N) = v_l(cond eps) >= 2 for existence of D, and the relation A^2 = eps_prim(l) l^{k-2}.
Remark (2) notes the consequent uniqueness of f, with coefficients generating the field of rationality of rho over F_p.
acceptance: Check that N is prime to p by construction and that n(l, rho) = dim V/V^{G_0} exactly in the tame case
Check the density-1 sufficiency of the trace identity by a Cebotarev argument on the finite image of rho

links.reason: Lemme 6.11 requires M free of finite type over the discrete valuation ring; in the application 6.10 M is the O_lambda-module of modular forms of type (k, eps) on Gamma_0(N). The freeness and finite generation of that module over O_lambda is exactly what the base-change theorem supplies, and only within its hypotheses (k >= 2, or k = 1 with small level).

Serre's property (3.1.6) - every common system of Hecke eigenvalues in F_p-bar lifts to characteristic zero - is justified in the source by an explicit citation to Deligne-Serre lemme 6.11, and it is what makes the definition of residual modularity by reduction from characteristic zero nonvacuous.

Deligne's representation rho_f is produced in 6.12 as a semisimplification of a reduction, a priori over the residue field of a large extension; Lemme 6.13 is what places it over the field k_f generated by the a_p and the reductions of eps(p), i.e. it is what makes 'a coefficient field and a prime over p' in the residual-modularity definition well posed.

The refined statement (3.2.4?) fixes eps and the class of k by det rho; the source establishes the compatibility (1.3.6) det rho(Frob_l) = l^{k-1} eps(l) only after Proposition 2 identifies h with k-1 mod (p-1).
